Counter-Strike 2 is one of the worst games you will ever play. Ive played 4k+ hours in CSGO split between 2 Accounts and enjoyed the game a lot before. Sure in the past the game always had somewhat of a cheater issue but back then it was maybe 1 cheater per 20-30 games or even less since it was not always so easy to tell if someone is cheating. As soon as someone went obvious they got banned in a somewhat short time. Now you sometimes have 10 games in a row with people cheating so obvious they even sometimes admit it. Some people spinbot on accounts that have between 500 and 1000 hours of playtime with no issue at all. if you have an enemie that "only" uses wh obviously by prefireing everything perfectly you are lucky since you have a chance relatively seen. The game is beyond dead because if you are a OBVIOUS cheater you are basically just an npc that gets farmed by cheaters. 

Without the huge cheater problem this game would be so great. Seriously the best shooter every made. But with the cheater problem its just unplayable. Ive played it for some weeks while accepting that i just get picket apart by cheater almost every game and tryed to still enjoy it but its just not acceptable anymore especially since you sometimes have cheaters that are even so arrogant that they mock you in all-chat with knowing you position etc. all the time. 

Ive uninstalled the game for now an probably forever like a lot of people have done and if you just watch the statistics then you will quickly realize that this game will most likely not have a comeback ever because its just going downhill from this point.

Pls just dont buy this game and safe your time money and inner peace

Wheatley, in particular, is a pleasant surprise in how well he actually fits as an antagonist in this game. A great replacement for GLaDOS (regardless of how much I love her as a character).  Going on from this, I love the dark and ruined environments in this game, and it really makes the original remnants stand out. You find out pretty early that the facility isn't as it used to be, but it's actually impressive how ruined the whole place is, and it's quite stunning at times. The inclusion of more in-depth lore about what the facility is and how each of the characters involved in it was my personal favourite part of the game, as it really develops the characters in unexpected ways. And, as expected, the game design is perfect. Each puzzle feels rewarding, satisfying and exhilarating to get right. You'd be missing out big time if you didn't play this.

review:
An absolute masterpiece of a game.

Stardew Valley is one of those games that I will always come back to, no matter how much time has passed. I have over 200 hours on PC alone, and I couldn't even begin to guess how many more I've spent playing on Switch! No matter how many times I start a new farm, there is always something new to discover, another goal to work toward, or another reason to fall in love with the game all over again.

The amount of content is genuinely incredible. Between the overarching story, the countless quests, the secrets to uncover, and the individual stories and relationships of each NPC, there is always something to do. Every character feels unique, with their own personality, struggles, interests, and growth. Getting to know the villagers and seeing their stories unfold makes Pelican Town feel like a real community rather than just a setting for a farming game.

And the farming itself? There is genuinely something for every type of player! review:
This game has a lot of content and it took me a long time to beat.  When I say "beat," I mean "perfect."  Because the only way to really beat the game is to 100% it, which is very time-consuming.

There's not really much of a story except for at the beginning.  Otherwise, you basically just build up your life, family, friends and town.  There are really only two mutually exclusive choices to make, but they mostly lead to similar outcomes, and the rewards are different.

When starting the game, you can choose what kind of farm you want between a regular farm, beach farm, a forage farm, a farm with monsters, etc.  The goal is still the same; sow, harvest, get paid.

I lost track of how many quests there were, mostly because a lot of them repeat.  If I were to summarize it into different parts, I'd limit it to the following:  Farming, mining, relationships and community.

Farming is what you would think; grow crops, build coops and stables, care for animals, produce artisan goods, craft stuff, cook dishes, etc.

Mining is more of the adventurous and combative part of the game where you explore the floors of mines, fight enemies, find rare resources and artifacts, forge, find and upgrade weapons, etc.

Relationships involve the local and non-local citizens.  Talking to them, gifting them things they like or completing quests for them increase your relationship.  In contrast, saying mean things, hitting trashcans in front of them, or gifting them things they don't like will decrease your relationship.  There are events that happen at various times and places once you've reached a certain relationship threshold with a particular person and it reveals a little more depth to their lives and develops their character further.  There are bachelors and bachelorettes that can be romanced and eventually married, after which they move in with you, enabling you to have/adopt up to 2 children.  Some of this cannot be done until you've upgraded your house sufficiently.  There are a number of characters that are either already married or cannot otherwise be romanced.  There are mods that can change this, FYI.  I didn't use any of them, for the record.

The community-related part of the game involves developments that improve things around town, like fixing buses, boats or bridges that lead to new places, fixing the greenhouse on your property for indoor farming, removing rocks so that ore and minerals flow through the town's water, etc.  This is the part where there are two mutually exclusive ways to go about it.  The developer has made it very apparent that one of these ways is their preferred way, and is a lot more in-depth and time-consuming in nature.  The other way is more efficient, but is made to feel more empty in the end.  Some of the new places revealed by these developments are beyond the local town, and there are different caves, mines, farms, people and quests to work with.  Like I said, this game has a lot of content.

I can see why so many people like this game.  I'd say the unfortunate part for me was that I got overwhelmed at one point and had to put it down.  I came back a few years later to complete it.  It's difficult to do this, however, because I had to remember how everything worked and how I left things originally. 

Anyway, I think most adventure gamers, or people who like games such as Terraria or Minecraft would enjoy this game a lot.

review:
Feels silly to leave a review on a game so well known as this, but gotta let CA know I appreciate his attitude towards fans. 

Lots of replayability because you can decide if you want to prioritize money, friendships, or resources at the start of your run as well as farm layouts, marriage options, pets/farm animals, etc. 

It's no secret that a lot of us hate the fishing mechanic so it would be nice if there was an option to adjust it outside of rod and equipment purchases. However there is a way to get to level 5 fishing without fishing much or using mods.

Community Center Completion tip: [spoiler]I complete bundles the best I can/want to for easy rewards/farm help and then purchase the joja membership and pay to complete the remaining ones (it's the fish tank lets be honest). Membership fee is still the same but you only have to pay to complete bundles you haven't already completed so the overall cost is much less than if purchased from the beginning. It will no longer be a community center but a joja mart warehouse or whatever, so be sure to consider that. [/spoiler]

Mastering Fishing: [spoiler]Use the crab pots and just fish wherever it's easiest for you to do so. Better rods and bait/bobbers are available eventually to help further. The REAL way to quickly do this is read books. The fishing books help obviously BUT there are a handful of books that will send xp points to other skills if the main skill it's meant to benefit is maxed. I mastered fishing this way within 4years without prioritizing it. Bookseller and traveling cart merchant are where to go. [/spoiler]

Pretty much anything else can be modded and CA has always openly supported the mod community. I recommend playing without mods as long as possible to best understand the game as many popular mods add a lot of new content and it can be overwhelming for new players.

review:
Act 1: Absolutely amazing. The absolute peak of RPG gaming.

Act 2: Still good, but the cracks are starting to show.

Act 3: An incomprehensible clusterfuck where everything pretends to matter, but somehow nothing feels particularly impactful anymore.

Baldur's Gate 3 starts off as one of the most incredible RPG experiences I've ever had. Act 1 is genuinely fantastic. The exploration, the companions, the choices, the feeling that you're just a bunch of adventurers trying to make sense of the world around you. It's everything I want from an RPG.

Act 2 is still good, but things start feeling increasingly railroaded. Misinterpret one little thing, make a decision without fully understanding its consequences, and suddenly something massive happens that can sour the rest of your campaign. Player agency starts feeling less like freedom and more like trying to guess what the writers intended you to do.

And then comes Act 3.

Good lord, what happened here?

Suddenly you're drowning in supposedly world-shattering revelations, grand conspiracies, and characters with increasingly ridiculous ambitions. Everything is presented as the most important thing imaginable, yet very little of it actually feels meaningful.

It's like starting out reading The Fellowship of the Ring, embarking on this wonderful, grounded adventure with a group of companions, only for the story to slowly transform into some American Gods-style drama where the biggest, strongest, most important beings in existence all have the biggest, meanest plans.

And of course, you and your merry band of increasingly overpowered superheroes are the only ones who can stop them.

Somewhere along the way, the grounded RPG adventure turns into a comical superhero flick.

And perhaps the funniest part is that, in doing so, Baldur's Gate 3 stays remarkably faithful to D&D 5e.

Because it suffers from exactly the same progression problem: you start out as a bunch of nobodies worrying about goblins stealing someone's chickens, and before you know it, you're fighting gods, dragons, and the equivalent of World War III because apparently every adventure needs to escalate into a cosmic catastrophe.

Bigger stakes, bigger villains, bigger explosions. But not necessarily a better story.

I wish Baldur's Gate 3 had remained the adventure it was in Act 1. A wonderful, personal journey where your companions, discoveries, and smaller decisions felt like they mattered.

Instead, it trades that magic for an increasingly bloated spectacle that seems convinced the fate of the entire universe is inherently more interesting than the fate of a handful of adventurers.

An absolutely phenomenal beginning, a decent middle, and a final act that completely lost me.

Sometimes saving a village from goblins is a far better adventure than saving the entire world from gods.

review:
Let's get one thing out of the way before I say anything: I adore this game. I adore the combat, the story, all the characters, and that I'm still finding new things in every playthrough. I'm on my 8th playthrough right now. You can see how many hours I have in this game. At the time of writing this review I have three more playthroughs planned not including the one I'm currently on. None have been boring and every single one has been different. I've played this game every three months since its release.

Now, would I recommend this game to other players? It depends.

Do you enjoy an intricate story with lots of character customization and role playing possibilities but don't care for intricate combat? Play this game and play it on the easiest difficulty. Look up builds so you know which abilities to pick and what gear to buy. Get mods to make your player character look even wackier or make them nigh invincible so the combat is peanuts. Romance your favorite companion and then make a new character and romance them again. Explore what happens when you fail a roll. Save scum if you don't like the outcome. Play your favorite character's origin and make them smooch another origin character, or your guardian. Make their guardian look like your player character. Take screenshots. Frame your favorites. Go wild. 

Do you enjoy strategy turn based combat that has a variety of ways to solve fights, challenging bosses and hours of enormous battles with 20+ participants, but don't care for elaborate party management, pesky approval ratings and their consequences, and don't care for role playing in general? Play this game on Tactician and only use hirelings, don't recruit any companions. Try honor mode and enjoy the adrenaline rush. Min-max your heart out. Do a challenge run. (Also definitely try the previous game from Larian; Divinity Original Sin 2 if you enjoy this type of combat.)

However. Do you not care for elaborate roleplay worth hundreds of hours over multiple playthroughs, long cutscenes and romance mechanics, or any form of turn-based strategy games? Then there's thousands of other games for you out there. But probably not this one.

Or, you know, get it on sale some time and give it a go anyway. Broaden your horizons.

review:
Really fun, but I hate fighting games. I really appreciate this game because it was a fighting game I could get into it. The amazing visuals & animation definitely pulled me in. The characters all have distinct personalities & great designs. The music is good too. 

Overall, I though the combat was great. The amazing art made it feel really good & look very cool. It is definitely accessible to get into, and I recommend it if you don't have experience with the genre (like me). Landing hits & winning just feels super satisfying in this game. 

However, I think fighting games still aren't for me. I'm just not the biggest fan of memorizing random inputs & hoping my directional inputs are even correct. These games just feel kind of restrictive to me, and I prefer being able to improvise with different tools. In addition, I think some characters just have super annoying combos. I've played a lot of games where I still had fun losing, but I just give up when somebody uses a character with some insane combo and I can't do anything. Also, I think too much of the roster is paid DLC. 

Still, I'm glad I gave this game a try & I did enjoy it a bit, but I got burnt out of it so quickly. I just don't think grinding to get good is gonna feel worth it or fun at all to me. I'll come to this game eventually.

review:
Emergence Day. That’s what they’re calling it.

I call it the day my pants permanently relocated to a higher tax bracket.
Out poured the Locust. Not “scary underground bugs.” Not “aggressive moles with attitude.” Full-grown, armor-plated, chainsaw-resistant nightmares that look like they were designed by a committee of angry gorillas.

You aim for the head. They aim for your entire bloodline.
You take cover. They remove the cover. With extreme prejudice. And then stand on the rubble looking offended that you thought concrete could stop them.
The little ones move faster than my will to live. One second you’re fine, the next you’re being used as a personal trampoline.

And the big ones… sweet mother of all that is holy. You hear that roar and suddenly every tactical doctrine you’ve ever learned gets replaced by pure, undiluted “RUN.” There’s no covering fire. There’s no flanking. There’s just you, your legs, and the sudden realization that “tactical retreat” is just a fancy way of saying “I am about to set a new land-speed record in combat boots.” The gunfire is loud. The chainsaws are louder. The Locust laughing while they turn your squad into confetti is somehow louder still. I’ve developed a permanent flinch response to any sudden noise. Brother, I’ve seen things. Things that would make a seasoned soldier hide under his bed and ask for his mommy. Things that make the phrase “emergence day” sound less like a historical event and more like the name of the therapy bill I’m still paying off.
Would I recommend it?

Absolutely.

Just bring extra underwear. And maybe a second pair for the first pair. And a third pair for the emotional support underwear.
Five stars.

Would get psychologically destroyed again.

For the COG

Anyway, now time for a short review. The movement in the game feels great. Yes yes, we liked how ridiculous the roadie run was and how wall bouncing was the unofficial Mexican citizenship test. However, the sprinting mechanics, the slides, just the overall fluidity of the game feel amazing and they did a great job.

Named characters aren't safe, and this game is just as brutal as it's previous titles. You thought Ben in Gears 2 was bad? Alright pal. The gore and atmosphere are amazing. Lancer sounds beefy, very important. Valen is the goat. We don't talka bout gears 4 and 5 horde...but anyway...E-Day makes horde into a 12 player objective based mode with some light base defense options for holdout spots. Considering the game takes place over two days, the Horde mode is essentially what other squads are doing during the first and second nights/days of the invasion. What's REALLY hype is all 3 fireteams engaging the bosses. You ever open your tacview and see the outlines of 11 other gears posted up in buildings shooting a Brumak? Well I have, and it's peak.

VERSUS.

Digression aside, absolutely recommended provided you've got a powerful PC that can handle UE5 games.

review:
Gears E-Day is a return to form. I’ve been playing Gears of War since 2008. Long time fan of this series but I’ve been lukewarm since The Coalition took over. Gears 4 was a perfectly fine game, which doesn’t live up to the original trilogy. Gears 5 is a horrible attempt at an open world with a horrible story to boot. 

E-Day feels like The Coalition finally listened to fans and took the steps to give us a game that’ll stand next to the original trilogy. 

Story:
Don’t believe what all the grifters are saying, this isn’t some weird bait and switch where Marcus and Dom are sidelined. Mags and Reyes are important characters but it’s no different than Cole and Baird in Gears 1. Mags and Reyes both get character arcs in the 3rd and 4th arc of the campaign. Their stories at   worst are whatever. Marcus and Dom’s brotherhood is what the story revolves around. So don’t listen to all the idiots who are just parroting what they heard online, this isn’t some attempt to push a political agenda where all the male leads are put in the corner. The “female protagonist” tag that got added to steam is insane. It’s on par with saying Gears 3 is woke because it added two female Gears into Marcus’ and Cole’s squad. 

Versus: 
A fun time all around. It feels like they’ve finally done away with wall bouncing. This game has the potential to keep more “casual” fans around which will keep the game alive longer. The weapons all feel fun to use. E-Day captures the feeling of the classic Gears multiplayer in a way that modern Halo games never could. The maps included are awesome and instant classics. 

Horde:
Interesting addition to the series. I like the missions in the semi open world areas. Running into other squads is fun and offers dynamic gameplay moments. I’ve had quite a few times were a random squad has rolled up and saved my squad from wiping or vice versa. I’d love to see another mode of horde similar to Gears of War 3 or 4. 

Customization/Live service:
As of right now, The Coalition has kept their promise. There is very few things that you can’t outright earn through gameplay. Plenty of skins and profile customizations are unvoiced through challenges or just playing the game. You earn the in game currency at a very fair rate. I had all the skins I wanted within 5-6 hours or playtime. I’m excited to see what each new season adds. I’d love to see more characters, maps and weapons added as time goes on.

TLDR:

If you’re a Gears of War fan, please get this. The Coalition really showed they’re capable of handling this franchise. Story mode is great, versus is fun and horde is a great time. Don’t listen to all the crybaby grifters.

review:
Not for $70 
Simple as that. The game is Gears of War, for sure. Gameplay is cool, environments are breath taking, like levels are look so good. I just can't find a lick of care. It just not good. Everytime I pick this game up to do the campaign I'm bored within like an hour which is insane. 
The story should be epic, emotional, gritty. It just doesn't give you a reason to really give a care about anyone. Sure humanity is under attack, that's it. Maybe I'm trippin', but I just don't care about running around open world esk maps trying to save civilians for nothing but a feel good in the context of a video game. 
The collectibles and hard cases (Weapon perk unlocks) found throughout the campaign just take away from the experience for me. So many times I've missed something happening in the game because I'm looking around to weapon unlocks or some random item they call a collectible and they provide like a couple sentences of world building.  
I actually like the characters, alot of folks hate Mag but as a veteran (non-combat) I get it, she makes sense, I don't dislike her but I'm confused as to why Dom isnt the guy always there for us..its Mags? I'm in act 4 of the campaign and know so little about her and her personality. She is incredibly one dimensional, disgruntled veteran and nothing else. Reyes is cool but he is incompetent until the story needs him to suddenly know how to do something. Dom is there. That's it. Dom's brother was killed in action and for some reason Marcus is the only one allowed to be emotional about it. Marcus constantly gets all depressed and sad whenever DOM the guy whos BLOOD BROTHER WAS KILLED brings up his OWN BROTHER. 
Just..somehow the most intense and lore rich 'last stand' of humanity in Gears history is just..boring

review:
Honestly, after the let downs from 4 and 5 this game was very MUCH a return to proper form and what I remembered when I first played Gears of War 20 years ago with my brothers. 

Does the game have its issues? 100%. 
Are they working on it? Yes.
Is it worth the current price? Absolutely. 

The campaign is strong, we are able to see and explore just how brutal and terrifying the locust war was. Versus is also fun, I just seem to have a massive skill gap with everyone else on the enemy team. I have not played the new horde siege but I heard that its you with your squad and two other squads in one game, so up to 12 players in a PvE environment. 

Gears of War is so back with this title, hopefully they can capture what exactly they did right so they can continue the story with this EXACT magic without having to ride everyone's nostalgia highs by bringing back fan favorite characters. Funny enough it almost seems like it was written and developed by some former Epic Games employees with how well crafted this story was and how familiar this game feels.

review: They did a lot to this game that I'm not a fan of and I'm not gonna get into it. But IMO they ruined the mechanics. the run system feels clunky, isn't bound to (A) any longer. (Y) to hurdle over cover... (A) used to make all the movements feel fluid. You no longer duck when running so its easier to take bullet fire as you cant duck under walls. Weapons also had a rework and everything is way to over powered, you cant react to power weapons or lancer fire like you used to now you just have to take the L if your in line of sight. Reload system also reworked you cant quick reload when active reloading you have to wait for every bullet to be inserted before you can active.... wow. Executions can now be contested so doing them isn't just a death wish now as you don't have a quick curb stomp- Your also feeding the enemy team and not securing your kill when pressing the button. If you choose to finish with a shotgun blast you better be on top of them I've gotten 3 shots off from 5 feet and not one killed someone once. Maybe they want to make this more appealing to an average player as the OG's often made the game unplayable to the noobies, but this is way to much and I know I'm missing a ton. If they were catering to a new player base I hope it pays off but this game isnt for me.

review:
As a longtime Gears fan who has played every game multiple times since 2012, I absolutely love this game.

This game has it all. The movement is incredibly smooth and honestly rivals games like TLOU2, the weapons feel great, and the story is fantastic. Seeing Marcus and Dom back together again is great, and I really like the new characters too. They might not be as iconic as Baird, Cole, and Anya, but they're still great additions to the series.

I also really like how they've experimented with a more open approach in certain sections. Being able to revisit previous areas and see how much more destroyed they become as the story progresses is such a cool detail. The boss fights have been really fun, and getting to experience the origins of the Locust War has been a highlight.

Now, I think it's only fair to address some of the complaints I've seen about this game.

First off, this game is not "woke." The game includes optional banners and flags that you can equip if you want to. That's it. If something as simple as optional cosmetics is enough to make you not recommend or not want to play a game, then honestly, you shouldn't be playing games.

I've also seen a lot of people complaining that The Coalition gives Lucas and Mags too much focus, which is just straight-up not true. Mags gets maybe five minutes of focus in a campaign that's over 12 hours long. The additional character details also make sense when you consider that the campaign now supports four-player co-op instead of the two-player co-op of the older games. Giving the new characters actual personalities and backstories makes it easier for players to care about whoever they're playing as. I really don't see the problem here.

As for the multiplayer, Versus is solid. Nothing particularly groundbreaking, but it's good. Horde is fun too, although I personally prefer how it was handled in the older games.

Now, for my dislikes, which honestly aren't many. I do think it was a mistake to remove some of the features that made the older games so unique. Meatshields, unique weapon executions, Lancer battles, and grenade tagging are all awesome mechanics that I wish had returned. These features added a lot of personality to the combat, and I would've loved to see them make a comeback.

That said, none of these complaints come close to ruining the experience for me.

I'd give this game a 9.5/10. The story is great, the characters are great, the movement feels fantastic, the weapons are satisfying, and the gameplay is just incredibly fun. It manages to feel like Gears of War while still trying new things, and I think The Coalition has done a fantastic job with it.

I'm extremely happy with what they've delivered. I really don't have any major complaints, and I can't wait to see where the series goes from here.

review:
Positives:

- Atmosphere feels like old Gears
- Smoother movement
- Longer overall game
- Plethora of characters (the more, the merrier)
- The return of unlocks through challenges. Thank you
- Great world building as a prequel to the post-apocalypse of the OG trilogy
- The soundtrack
- Best new type of horde that never knew I needed (helldivers-esque). Makes me actually fee like a COG soldier fighting in the war effort instead of just your basic survival mode

Negatives:

- Still noticed the performative activism. In the universe of Gears of War (or any other form of fictional media), inclusion should not be forced upon gamers or anyone who is just trying to escape from reality and enjoy a good, fantasized story. On that note, who cares about a visual lecture of inclusion? Especially in Gears where both men and women are already strong together. All are badasses suffering in a world they are trying to fight for. That's all that matters. I guarantee you that people who made all these games in the 00s did not even think about representation of current, real world issues at the time. Instead, they just cared about making a fun game that rocks your world and nothing more. Of course there are influences (everything comes from something), but only for the sake of making something fresh and cool. But at least it was just performative activism and not something like corporate pandering, preachy tones, or something worse. Maybe I didn't notice or it flew over my head as I was just trying to really immerse myself. Maybe there's a hint of tokenism. Who knows? I would have to replay it. Either way these things would only matter if a story calls for it (like an actual political story, a non-established story that has these elements as the plot points, and so on). Not for Gears of War. Only in it for the gore, the right use of profanity, the affliction, the rage, the vengeance, the savagery, the survival, and the cooperation against monsters for the possibility of peace

- Missed opportunities: meat shields, chainsaw duels, different execution animation for each gun, and more

- Absolutely love longer games, but for Gears, not too much a fan of the semi-open world maps. Just like old Halo, I mostly prefer a linear playthrough. Don't be a try hard like Ubisoft with innovation. Just keep Gears of War consistent with only minor upgrades. Horde Siege is the only good innovation.


Overall, a 7 out of 10. The positives pretty much outweighs the big 3 negatives for me personally. This installment seems somewhat consistent. Just be careful with contracting new hires. I would prefer dedicated employees who are passionate nerds/fans of the games instead of someone who is just getting by. That's for elsewhere, not passion projects. There could've been more opportunities for this game, especially unique mechanics from the older games. And don't try hard to think of something new, only once in a blue moon. Instead, be excited building upon what's there bit by bit. Again, even though I noticed the activism (the biggest of the negatives), it is not as bad as worse titles out there (Dragon Age Veilguard and the recent Halo Campaign Evolved remake for instance).

review:
[[h2]The Worst FIFA Yet.[/h2]

As someone who has been a loyal FIFA fan for over 20 years, it's genuinely disappointing to see how far this franchise has fallen. I've watched the game progressively get worse year after year, and somehow EA continues to find ways to disappoint.

[hr][/hr]

[b]FIFA no longer rewards actual soccer knowledge or strategy.[/b]

What used to be a game built around tactical awareness, intelligent positioning, and strategic play has turned into an unrealistic arcade experience centered around excessive dribbling, through  balls, and exploiting fast-paced players.

Instead of rewarding players who understand the sport, the game rewards those who master repetitive, unrealistic mechanics, and I've realized this because I have gotten better at the game but it is no longer as satisfying. Defending has become a frustrating game of chasing down opponents who constantly abuse pace and dribbling. [b]It's no longer about outsmarting your opponent with soccer IQ, but about exploiting the game's mechanics to an extreme way and everyone I have had try out this game that have played FIFA for years have expressed similar frustrations.[/b]

I understand EA wanted to overhaul the defending system to make a wider skill game but they ruined the game, there should be a reasonable middle ground between skill-based defending and realistic gameplay. Instead they've made defending unnecessarily frustrating and completely disrupted the balance that once made FIFA enjoyable.

[hr][/hr]

[b]The gameplay itself is another disappointment.[/b]

The game is inconsistent, has many bugs, and instead of fixing the same problems players have complained for years, EA continues releasing what feels like the same broken product with a new title. 

What used to be one of my favorite games has turned into a frustrating , poorly optimized mess. After more than two decades of supporting this franchise, this is my first review and I would just like to say again it is embarrassing to see the direction it has taken. 

[h3]Easily the worst FIFA I've played. Would not recommend.[/h3]

review:
[h1] When everything works, the game is great. Unfortunately, nothing ever really fully works. [/h1]

I'll add some context here: this is the first FIFA/FC I've played in around 4–5 years, so coming back to the series has genuinely been fun. However, the sheer amount of technical issues is, quite honestly, embarrassing.

You'd think that after making essentially the same game every year for well over 20 years, something as simple as the menus actually working would be a fair expectation, but apparently not.

Other issues include the game randomly deciding, after starting a match, that you're now playing with MnK instead of your controller. The best part? The controller will still work perfectly fine in the menus, just not in the actual match. The amount of times the only solution to something in this game is to simply turn it off and back on again is astounding.

Then there's the servers. Every 4–5 games, they'll seemingly just collapse, and you'll be handed a loss regardless of whether you were winning or not. I've even had a game where I was 3–0 up, my opponent left, and somehow [b] I was handed the loss?[/b] Where is the logic in that?

The new co-op mode, "The Grounds", is actually a lot of fun, but again, it comes with the usual preface of [i]"when it works"[/i], which seems to be a 50/50 coin flip every time you launch it. The stability in The Grounds is shocking as well. Random frame drops down to 20–30 FPS before shooting straight back up to 100+, regardless of how high or low your graphics settings are. There is seemingly no rhyme or reason to it.

I write all of this knowing full well that I'll continue playing because, underneath all the issues, I am genuinely having fun with the game. When everything is working as intended, it's a fun game.

But in terms of recommending that someone else spends their money on it? [u]Absolutely not.[/u]

I can't buy the whole [i]"Oh well, it's an EA game, what do you expect?"[/i] excuse either. At the end of the day I have paid for a game that can barely manage to function consistently, despite being an annual release from one of the biggest publishers in the industry.

It's a shambles the majority of the time, the fact that there's a genuinely enjoyable game buried underneath all of it just makes it that much more frustrating.
